blocks.p: Turning a mod off in the *Mods* window changes the main mod list, which is used for new games only. Saves keep their own mod lists, opened from *Load game*, *More*, *Choose mods*.

In a save's own list, *If you turn it off* at the foot of the mod's *About* tab says what turning the mod off would do to that save. It rates the change *Careful* or *Not safe for a game in progress* and gives the reasons, as listed in Table 59-1.

table.label: Table 59-1
table.title: What a save loses when a mod is turned off
head: The mod adds
In the save
rows: They disappear: from you, your bags, containers and the ground.
They go away. What you made stays, unless it is one of its own items.
What it changed goes back to the game's version.
A character may lose one of its traits.
Kept in the save, unused, until the mod is back.
Its places are empty; a character there can load into nothing.
Anything built or placed from them goes missing.

blocks.note: A map or tiles make a mod not safe.

blocks.p: Figure 59-1 shows the pane for a mod that adds items, recipes and settings of its own. The pane marks it *Careful*.
In a save's own list the pane speaks for that save. A mod that is not safe for it asks first, in the band at the foot of the window. Click *Turn off* to turn it off, or *Cancel* to leave it on.

blocks.p: To turn a mod off, click *Turn off* in its info pane.

marks.text: Saves keep their own mod lists, so the main list changes new games only.
Careful: the pane lists what the save would lose, reason by reason.
In a save's own list the pane speaks for that save: a map or tiles make it not safe, with the reasons.
A mod that is not safe asks first, in the band at the window's foot.
